newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro-bourses boosted by Santa Claus rally.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro-bourses boosted by Santa Claus rally.

text.p: Major European bourses forged ahead on Friday after a "Santa Claus rally" in the United States sent Wall Street surging two percent.
London's FTSE 100 index opened at a record high while France's CAC 40 and Germany's DAX indices also latched onto Wall Street's coat tails.
"The Dow's jump overnight was unbelievable. It certainly has given the market a boost in confidence," one senior dealer in London said.
British and German government bonds both opened confidently, boosted by a strong bond rally in the United States.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar was little changed but analysts said the outlook remained bullish, with a raft of European economic data on Friday pointing to slow growth and benign price pressures across the continent.
The U.S. bond rally helped the Dow Jones industrial average to soar 126.87 points to 6,473.64 overnight in its second biggest point gain ever.
"This may be the start of the Santa Claus rally," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at U.S.-based Legg Mason Wood Walker.
After recent jittery performances by stock markets, Wall Street's surge came as a morale boost for European bourses.

Britain's FTSE 100 index of leading shares opened 45.1 points higher at 4,096.4. But mild profit-taking and the expiration of FTSE index futures and options contracts nudged prices off their earlier all-time highs.
By 1215 GMT the FTSE was at 4,083.1, up 31.8 points or 0.78 percent.
"The market is still sorting itself out now that the expiration time has passed. If Wall Street comes in with another good start, we could re-test the highs later today," one trader said.
When the FTSE's previous intraday trading high of 4,094.4, was reached on November 26, shares quickly retreated, ending the day at 4,068.4.
But another strong showing on Wall Street may be enough to keep the FTSE above its previous closing record of 4,073.1, dealers said.

"A new closing high is definitely within sight after the Dow rally," the head of sales and trading at a large brokerage said. "An assault on the 4,100 level is also possible today but we may fall a bit short."

Car-components company GKN failed to join the pre-Christmas rally, however, falling 20 pence to 989.5 following Thursday's U.S. court ruling which may cost the company 331 million pounds ($553 million).
German shares opened floor trading strongly higher, boosted like bourses elsewhere by the Wall Street rally but also helped by a strong government bond market. Prices later shaded lower.
"The firm dollar, Wall Street and Bunds are all responsible for taking us into the heavens," said one dealer.
The rally was spearheaded by the car sector including BMW AG, Volkswagen and Daimler-Benz, which saw the 30-share DAX index rise 1.5 percent to 2,850 by 1215 GMT.
In Paris, shares added one percent to the CAC index in opening trades, building on Wall Street's overnight run.

Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel weakened to a low of 6.85 francs before recovering to stand 0.7 percent down at 6.95, following Thursday's small fire on a platform at the Folkestone terminal, which was quickly put out.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar was slightly softer against the mark and slightly firmer against the yen as traders wound down ahead of the holiday.

"If it is possible to discern a theme from today it's that there is still a strong chance of further repo cuts in Germany and, while all of Europe is tigthening fiscally, core European currencies should cheapen against the dollar," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5560 marks and 114.28 yen, compared with 1.5597 marks and 114.07 yen in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1215 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 31.8 points, or 0.78 percent, at 4,083.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 34.09, or 1.52 percent, at 2,282.79.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 42.75 points, or 1.52 percent, at 2,850.5.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $369.20, up 20 cents on the previous fixing. Silver was marked up a cent behind gold at $4.87.
